```{ojs}
//| output: false
// VM is the shared utility library, loaded on every page by the mathviz
// extension. This page uses VM.distributions (sampleStats, studentTCdf,
// fCdf), VM.sampling (seededRandom,
// gaussianRandom), VM.plotting (persistentPlot, draggablePoints, colors,
// alpha) and VM.ui (statRow, renderTable).
VM = window.VM

vmTheme = Generators.observe(notify => VM.plotting.onThemeChange(notify))

chartColors = VM.plotting.colors(vmTheme)

// The query string as the page was loaded, read once: each control takes its
// starting value from it. The two urlSync cells write it back.
urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)

// paramNumber: a URL parameter as a number in [lo, hi], or `fallback` when
// it is missing or not a number (a hand-edited or stale link).
function paramNumber(key, fallback, lo, hi) {
  const raw = urlParams.get(key)
  if (raw === null) return fallback
  const value = Number(raw)
  if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return fallback
  return Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, value))
}

function paramInt(key, fallback, lo, hi) {
  return Math.round(paramNumber(key, fallback, lo, hi))
}

function mean(values) {
  let sum = 0
  for (const v of values) sum += v
  return sum / values.length
}

// A fixed, evenly spread vertical offset for the i-th point of a group
// (the golden-ratio sequence), so a strip plot's points don't sit on one
// horizontal line and don't jump around between redraws.
function jitter(i) {
  return ((i * 0.6180339887) % 1 - 0.5) * 0.25
}

// A strip plot row's violin: the kernel density estimate of `values`
// (Gaussian kernel, Silverman's bandwidth on the SD `sd`), mirrored about the
// row's line y = row, as a filled Plotly trace. Only the shape matters, so
// every violin is scaled to the same widest point (0.4 of a row either
// side) whatever its height. It spans the data plus two bandwidths each
// side, as Plotly's own violins do, clipped to `range`, rather than a
// hairline across the whole axis.
function violinTrace(values, row, sd, color, range) {
  const steps = 200
  const halfWidth = 0.4
  const h = 1.06 * sd * values.length ** -0.2
  const lo = Math.max(range[0], Math.min(...values) - 2 * h)
  const hi = Math.min(range[1], Math.max(...values) + 2 * h)
  const xs = []
  const ds = []
  for (let i = 0; i <= steps; i++) {
    const x = lo + (hi - lo) * i / steps
    let sum = 0
    for (const v of values) {
      const z = (x - v) / h
      sum += Math.exp(-0.5 * z * z)
    }
    xs.push(x)
    ds.push(sum)
  }
  const peak = Math.max(...ds)
  const upper = ds.map(d => row - halfWidth * d / peak)
  const lower = ds.map(d => row + halfWidth * d / peak)
  return {
    x: [...xs, ...xs.slice().reverse(), xs[0]],
    y: [...upper, ...lower.slice().reverse(), upper[0]],
    type: "scatter", mode: "lines", fill: "toself", showlegend: false,
    fillcolor: VM.plotting.alpha(color, 0.12),
    line: {color, width: 1.5}, hoverinfo: "skip"
  }
}

function fmtP(p) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(p)) return "—"
  if (p < 1e-4) return "< 0.0001"
  return p.toFixed(4)
}

function fmt(v, digits = 2) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(v)) return "—"
  return v.toFixed(digits)
}
```

## The trouble with pairwise t-tests

<!-- TODO(text): with k groups there are k(k-1)/2 pairs; each test has a 5% false-alarm rate; the chance of at least one false alarm grows quickly. Every group in the app comes from the same population, so every significant pair is a false alarm. -->

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// One experiment drives both apps: k groups of n values, each drawn from
// N(mu, sigma^2), so H0 holds and every significant pairwise test is a
// false alarm until a group is dragged. Each group's mean is a drag handle
// in both apps, sitting exactly on the group's sample mean: dragging it
// shifts the group's points, in both apps, so their mean stays under it.
// Either app's "Redraw points" draws a fresh sample for both and puts the
// handles on its sample means.
model = ({
  k: 10,
  n: 50,
  mu: 50,
  sigma: 10,
  alpha: 0.05,
  // Chosen so the page opens on a draw where the pairwise tests go wrong:
  // draw 1, undragged, has 5 significant pairs (smallest p ~ 0.0005),
  // while ANOVA's p ~ 0.22 accepts H0.
  seed: 1004,
  valueRange: [0, 100],
  // Where a group's mean can be dragged: mean +/- 3 sigma stays on the
  // chart.
  meanRange: [30, 70]
})

// Draw d's noise (1-based), as k arrays of n standard normal values.
// Seeded per draw, so a draw's number in the URL reproduces it exactly.
function drawNoise(d) {
  const gauss = VM.sampling.gaussianRandom(VM.sampling.seededRandom(model.seed + 7919 * (d - 1)))
  const noise = []
  for (let g = 0; g < model.k; g++) {
    const z = new Array(model.n)
    for (let i = 0; i < model.n; i++) z[i] = gauss()
    noise.push(z)
  }
  return noise
}

// Draw d's sample as drawn, before any drag: k arrays of n values from
// N(mu, sigma^2).
drawSample = d => drawNoise(d).map(z => z.map(v => model.mu + model.sigma * v))

// The pooled two-sample t statistic for two groups of the same size n.
function pooledT(a, b, n) {
  const pooledVariance = (a.variance + b.variance) / 2
  return (a.mean - b.mean) / Math.sqrt(pooledVariance * 2 / n)
}

initialDraw = paramInt("draw", 1, 1, 1e9)

// The group means from the URL ("50.27,49.95,..."), k of them, each in
// meanRange; otherwise the starting draw's own sample means, undragged.
initialMeans = {
  const raw = urlParams.get("means")
  if (raw !== null) {
    const ms = raw.split(",").map(Number)
    if (ms.length === model.k && ms.every(Number.isFinite)) {
      const [lo, hi] = model.meanRange
      return ms.map(m => Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, m)))
    }
  }
  return drawSample(initialDraw).map(mean)
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// draw: which draw of the noise is on screen, 1-based -- the URL's, plus
// one per click of either app's "Redraw points".
draw = initialDraw + pwRedraw + avRedraw

sample = drawSample(draw)

groupMeans = avMeans.map(p => p.x)

// The experiment on screen, shared by both apps: every group's values, their
// summaries, every pairwise t-test, and the one-way ANOVA. With equal group
// sizes the pooled within-group variance is the average of the groups'
// variances, and F = (variance of the group means) / (pooled variance / n).
experiment = {
  const {k, n} = model
  // Each group as drawn, shifted so its sample mean is its handle.
  const groups = sample.map((values, g) => {
    const shift = groupMeans[g] - mean(values)
    return values.map(v => v + shift)
  })
  const stats = groups.map(v => VM.distributions.sampleStats(v))
  const df = 2 * n - 2
  const pairs = []
  let significant = 0
  for (let i = 1; i < k; i++) {
    for (let j = 0; j < i; j++) {
      const t = pooledT(stats[i], stats[j], n)
      const p = 2 * (1 - VM.distributions.studentTCdf(Math.abs(t), df))
      if (p < model.alpha) significant++
      pairs.push({i, j, t, p})
    }
  }
  const means = stats.map(st => st.mean)
  const grand = mean(means)
  let ss = 0
  for (const m of means) ss += (m - grand) ** 2
  const pooledVar = mean(stats.map(st => st.variance))
  const varMeans = ss / (k - 1)
  const chanceVar = pooledVar / n
  const F = varMeans / chanceVar
  const df1 = k - 1
  const df2 = k * (n - 1)
  const anova = {
    k, n, means, grand, pooledVar, varMeans, chanceVar, F, df1, df2,
    p: 1 - VM.distributions.fCdf(F, df1, df2),
    ssBetween: n * ss,
    ssWithin: (n - 1) * k * pooledVar
  }
  return {groups, stats, pairs, significant, anova}
}

// Keeps the draw and the group means in the address bar, the means to two
// decimals (a link shifts a group by at most 0.005). Reads the current
// query string rather than urlParams, so it keeps an embed= value.
urlSync = {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
  params.set("draw", String(draw))
  params.set("means", groupMeans.map(m => m.toFixed(2)).join(","))
  history.replaceState(null, "", `${window.location.pathname}?${params}`)
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// One color per group, shared by every chart on the page, so a reader can
// follow each group's points from one into the next. Ten groups need ten
// hues, more than the site palette's eight, so this is Tableau's ten-color
// scheme, legible on both themes.
groupColors = d3.schemeTableau10

groupIds = Array.from({length: model.k}, (_, g) => g + 1)

// The strip plot and the p-value matrix: two charts in one holder, side by
// side on a wide screen and stacked on a phone (.anova-duo). The strip plot
// runs values along x, like the pooled chart above it, and groups down y,
// group 1 on top like the matrix's rows. Both axes are fixed by k and
// valueRange, so a redraw or a drag never rescales them.
pwStripPlot = VM.plotting.persistentPlot({aspectRatio: 0.75, maxHeight: "760px"})

pwMatrixPlot = VM.plotting.persistentPlot({aspectRatio: 1, maxHeight: "420px"})
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Paints both pairwise charts: the strip plot (the same figure as the ANOVA
// app's, see stripFigure) and the p-value matrix, into its holder.
pwPaint = {
  const c = chartColors
  const G = model.k
  const {pairs} = experiment

  pwStripPlot(...stripFigure())

  // ── p-value matrix ──
  // Every group against every group, 1..G both ways and symmetric: cell
  // (i, j) and (j, i) are the same test. z is 1 for a significant pair, 0
  // otherwise, and -1 on the diagonal (a group against itself, no test),
  // which gets the faintest fill and a dash.
  const ids = []
  for (let g = 1; g <= G; g++) ids.push(g)
  const z = ids.map((_, r) => ids.map((_, col) => r === col ? -1 : null))
  const custom = ids.map(() => ids.map(() => "no test"))
  const annotations = []
  for (let g = 1; g <= G; g++) {
    annotations.push({x: g, y: g, text: "–", showarrow: false, font: {size: 9, color: c.muted}})
  }
  for (const {i, j, p} of pairs) {
    const sig = p < model.alpha
    let text = p.toFixed(2).replace(/^0/, "")
    // "<.01" is a character wider than the rest; a size smaller keeps it
    // inside its cell.
    let size = 9
    if (p < 0.01) {
      text = "<.01"
      size = 8
    }
    for (const [r, col] of [[i, j], [j, i]]) {
      z[r][col] = sig ? 1 : 0
      custom[r][col] = fmtP(p)
      annotations.push({
        x: col + 1, y: r + 1, text, showarrow: false,
        font: {size, color: sig ? c.halo : c.ink}
      })
    }
  }
  const faint = VM.plotting.alpha(c.muted, 0.08)
  const plain = VM.plotting.alpha(c.muted, 0.25)
  pwMatrixPlot([{
    type: "heatmap", x: ids, y: ids, z, customdata: custom,
    zmin: -1, zmax: 1, showscale: false, xgap: 2, ygap: 2,
    colorscale: [[0, faint], [0.5, plain], [1, c.alt]],
    hovertemplate: "group %{y} vs group %{x}<br>p = %{customdata}<extra></extra>"
  }], {
    showlegend: false, dragmode: false,
    title: {text: "p-value of each pairwise t-test", font: {size: 13}},
    // Square cells: scaleanchor ties the axes' scales, and constrain:
    // "domain" shrinks the wider axis's extent rather than padding its range
    // with empty space, which left a gap between the y labels and the first
    // column. No axis lines; the tick marks are transparent, there only to
    // hold the labels a few pixels off the cells.
    xaxis: {range: [0.5, G + 0.5], tickvals: ids, fixedrange: true, showgrid: false, zeroline: false, showline: false, ticks: "outside", ticklen: 4, tickcolor: "rgba(0,0,0,0)", side: "top", constrain: "domain"},
    yaxis: {range: [G + 0.5, 0.5], tickvals: ids, fixedrange: true, showgrid: false, zeroline: false, showline: false, ticks: "outside", ticklen: 4, tickcolor: "rgba(0,0,0,0)", scaleanchor: "x", constrain: "domain"},
    annotations,
    margin: {t: 60}
  })

  if (pwMatrixPlot.div.parentNode !== pwMatrixHolder) pwMatrixHolder.append(pwMatrixPlot.div)
}
```

// sample means, like the ANOVA app's own "Redraw points" (see draw and

```{ojs}
// All k * n values in one pile, before any split into groups, under their
// kernel density estimate (Gaussian kernel, Silverman's bandwidth on the
// pooled values' SD), so the curve follows the data as groups are dragged
// apart. Each point sits at a fixed fraction of the curve's height,
// colored by its group: while H0 holds, every color spreads across the whole
// bell, one sample. Both axes are fixed, so a redraw or a drag never
// rescales; a peak taller than the axis (a narrower pile than any the
// handles allow) would be clipped.
pwPooled = {
  const c = chartColors
  const points = []
  experiment.groups.forEach((values, g) => {
    for (const value of values) points.push({value, group: g + 1})
  })
  const values = points.map(d => d.value)
  const h = 1.06 * VM.distributions.sampleStats(values).sd * values.length ** -0.2
  const norm = 1 / (values.length * h * Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI))
  const density = x => {
    let sum = 0
    for (const v of values) {
      const z = (x - v) / h
      sum += Math.exp(-0.5 * z * z)
    }
    return sum * norm
  }
  const [lo, hi] = model.valueRange
  const curve = []
  for (let i = 0; i <= 200; i++) {
    const x = lo + (hi - lo) * i / 200
    curve.push({x, y: density(x)})
  }
  points.forEach((d, i) => {
    d.height = (0.04 + 0.92 * ((i * 0.6180339887) % 1)) * density(d.value)
  })
  return Plot.plot(VM.plotting.plotOptions({
    width, height: 300, marginLeft: 50,
    x: {domain: model.valueRange, label: `value (all ${model.k} groups pooled)`},
    y: {domain: [0, 0.045], label: "density"},
    clip: true,
    color: {type: "ordinal", domain: groupIds, range: groupColors, legend: true, label: "group"},
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(curve, {x: "x", y: "y", fill: c.muted, fillOpacity: 0.15}),
      Plot.dot(points, {
        x: "value", y: "height", fill: "group", r: 2.5, fillOpacity: 0.85,
        title: d => `group ${d.group}: ${d.value.toFixed(1)}`
      }),
      Plot.lineY(curve, {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: c.ink, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: c.muted})
    ]
  }))
}
```

```{ojs}
// Under the charts: each procedure's verdict on H0 (all k true means equal)
// for the points on screen -- the pairwise procedure rejects when any one of
// its tests does. Until a group is dragged, every group is drawn from one
// population, so every rejection is a false alarm.
pwStats = {
  const k = model.k
  const pairCount = k * (k - 1) / 2
  const verdict = rejected => rejected ? "H0 rejected" : "H0 not rejected"
  return VM.ui.statRow([
    {label: "Sig. pairs", value: `${experiment.significant} of ${pairCount}`, title: "Pairwise t-tests significant at 5% for the points on screen"},
    {label: "Pairwise", value: verdict(experiment.significant > 0), title: `H0 is rejected when at least one of the ${pairCount} pairwise t-tests is significant at 5%`},
    {label: "ANOVA", value: verdict(experiment.anova.p < model.alpha), title: `The single ANOVA F-test of all ${k} groups at 5%: p = ${fmtP(experiment.anova.p)}`},
  ])
}
```

## Variance between groups, variance within groups

<!-- TODO(text): ANOVA's picture -- the spread of the group means against the spread inside the groups. The points are the ones above; drag a group's mean and its group moves in both apps. -->

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Each app's drag handles on its strip plot: each group's sample mean,
// dragged left and right (or focused and moved with the arrow keys),
// carrying the group's points with it. y is pinned to the group; a drag
// snaps x to half units.
meanHandles = plot => VM.plotting.draggablePoints(plot, {
  value: initialMeans.map((m, g) => ({x: m, y: g + 1})),
  label: "Mean of group",
  color: groupColors.slice(0, model.k),
  xBounds: model.meanRange,
  yBounds: [0.5, model.k + 0.5],
  step: {x: 0.5, y: 1},
  constrain: (p, index) => ({x: Math.round(2 * p.x) / 2, y: index + 1}),
  format: (p, index) => `group ${index + 1}, mean ${p.x.toFixed(2)}`
})

// Created once, in a cell that depends on nothing reactive: the draggable
// means (viewof avMeans) and the paint cell share its div.
avPlot = VM.plotting.persistentPlot({aspectRatio: 0.9, maxHeight: "800px"})

// The strip plot both apps draw, as [data, layout] for a persistentPlot:
// each group's points with its violin, the grand mean, and, with `band`
// (the ANOVA app only), the chance band. No legend: every layer always
// shows. The group means are the handles, not traces.
function stripFigure({band = false} = {}) {
  const c = chartColors
  const {groups, stats, anova} = experiment
  const {k, grand, chanceVar} = anova
  const data = []

  // Where the group means would land if every group had the same true mean:
  // the grand mean +/- 2 standard errors, sqrt(pooled variance / n) each.
  // Colored by the F-test's verdict, so it always agrees with the ANOVA
  // readouts: green while H0 is not rejected, red once it is. Not by whether
  // every mean is inside: the F-test weighs all the means' spread together,
  // so several means near the edges can reject with all of them inside,
  // and one stray mean out of many can leave H0 standing.
  if (band) {
    const half = 2 * Math.sqrt(chanceVar)
    const bandColor = anova.p < model.alpha ? c.alt : c.ok
    data.push({
      x: [grand - half, grand - half, grand + half, grand + half, grand - half], y: [0.5, k + 0.5, k + 0.5, 0.5, 0.5],
      type: "scatter", mode: "lines", fill: "toself", showlegend: false,
      fillcolor: VM.plotting.alpha(bandColor, 0.08), line: {color: VM.plotting.alpha(bandColor, 0.5), width: 1}, hoverinfo: "skip"
    })
  }

  // Each group's violin (see violinTrace, on the group's own SD).
  for (let g = 0; g < k; g++) data.push(violinTrace(groups[g], g + 1, stats[g].sd, groupColors[g], model.valueRange))

  for (let g = 0; g < k; g++) {
    data.push({
      x: groups[g], y: groups[g].map((_, i) => g + 1 + jitter(i)),
      type: "scatter", mode: "markers", showlegend: false,
      marker: {color: groupColors[g], size: 6, opacity: 0.75},
      hovertemplate: `group ${g + 1}<br>%{x:.1f}<extra></extra>`
    })
  }

  data.push({
    x: [grand, grand], y: [0.5, k + 0.5], type: "scatter", mode: "lines", showlegend: false,
    line: {color: c.ink, width: 1.5, dash: "dash"}, hoverinfo: "skip"
  })

  const ticks = []
  for (let g = 1; g <= k; g++) ticks.push(g)
  return [data, {
    showlegend: false, hovermode: "closest", dragmode: false,
    xaxis: {title: "value", range: model.valueRange, fixedrange: true, zeroline: false},
    yaxis: {range: [k + 0.5, 0.5], tickvals: ticks, ticktext: ticks.map(g => `group ${g}`), fixedrange: true, showgrid: false, zeroline: false},
    margin: {t: 20}
  }]
}

// Either "Redraw points" also puts the handles on the new draw's own sample
// means, undoing any drag, so a redraw is a fresh experiment under H0. Set
// on the ANOVA app's handles; meansLink carries it to the pairwise app's.
// A native listener on each button, attached once; the buttons' values are
// already counted when their "input" fires.
redrawResetsMeans = {
  const reset = () => {
    const d = initialDraw + (viewof pwRedraw).value + (viewof avRedraw).value
    const means = drawSample(d).map(mean)
    const view = viewof avMeans
    view.value = means.map((m, g) => ({x: m, y: g + 1}))
    view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  }
  for (const button of [viewof pwRedraw, viewof avRedraw]) button.addEventListener("input", reset)
}

// Keeps the two apps' handles together: a drag in either sets the other's
// value and fires its "input", so its cells re-run too. A native listener
// on each, attached once (see CLAUDE.md); the equality check stops the
// mirrored event from bouncing back.
meansLink = {
  const same = (u, v) => u.length === v.length && u.every((p, i) => p.x === v[i].x)
  const mirror = (from, to) => from.addEventListener("input", () => {
    if (same(from.value, to.value)) return
    to.value = from.value
    to.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  })
  mirror(viewof avMeans, viewof pwMeans)
  mirror(viewof pwMeans, viewof avMeans)
}
```

```{ojs}
avStats = {
  const a = experiment.anova
  return VM.ui.statRow([
    {label: "Var(means)", value: fmt(a.varMeans, 1), title: "The sample variance of the group means: how far apart they are"},
    {label: "s²/n", value: fmt(a.chanceVar, 1), title: "How much the group means would vary if every group had the same true mean: the pooled within-group variance divided by the group size"},
    {label: "F", value: fmt(a.F, 2), title: `F = variance of the means / (s²/n), with ${a.df1} and ${a.df2} degrees of freedom`},
    {label: "p-value", value: fmtP(a.p), title: "The chance of an F at least this large if every group had the same true mean"},
    {label: "ANOVA", value: a.p < model.alpha ? "H0 rejected" : "H0 not rejected", title: "H0: every group has the same true mean. Rejected when the p-value is below 5%."}
  ])
}
```

```{ojs}
anovaTable = {
  const a = experiment.anova
  const dfTotal = a.k * a.n - 1
  return VM.ui.renderTable({
    html,
    headers: ["Source", "Sum of squares", "df", "Mean square", "F", "p-value"],
    filename: "anova-table.csv",
    rows: [
      ["Between groups", fmt(a.ssBetween, 1), String(a.df1), fmt(a.ssBetween / a.df1, 2), fmt(a.F, 3), fmtP(a.p)],
      ["Within groups", fmt(a.ssWithin, 1), String(a.df2), fmt(a.ssWithin / a.df2, 2), "", ""],
      ["Total", fmt(a.ssBetween + a.ssWithin, 1), String(dfTotal), "", "", ""]
    ]
  })
}
```

## Why variance tells us about means

<!-- TODO(text): the non-trivial reason. Under H0 the group means are k draws from N(mu, sigma^2/n), so their sample variance estimates sigma^2/n; the within-group variance estimates sigma^2 whether or not H0 holds. Comparing means = asking whether the means vary more than sigma^2/n allows, so the test statistic is a ratio of two variance estimates: n * Var(means) / s_p^2 = MS_between / MS_within. -->

## How fast false alarms pile up

<!-- TODO(text): with k groups there are m = k(k-1)/2 pairwise tests; if each had its own independent 5% chance of a false alarm, the chance of at least one is 1 - 0.95^m. ANOVA is one test, so it stays at 5% for every k. (The pairwise tests share groups, so they aren't independent, and the true rate sits a little below this curve; the shape is the same.) -->

```{ojs}
// The false-alarm rate against the number of groups k, in theory: some
// pairwise t-test rejects, 1 - (1 - alpha)^m with m = k(k-1)/2 tests treated
// as independent, against the single ANOVA F-test's alpha. No inputs: a
// fixed chart of the formula.
rateChart = {
  const c = chartColors
  const rows = []
  for (let k = 2; k <= 20; k++) {
    const m = k * (k - 1) / 2
    rows.push({k, m, rate: 1 - (1 - model.alpha) ** m, procedure: "Pairwise t-tests"})
    rows.push({k, m, rate: model.alpha, procedure: "ANOVA"})
  }
  return Plot.plot(VM.plotting.plotOptions({
    width, height: 320, marginLeft: 50,
    x: {domain: [2, 20], label: "number of groups k", ticks: 10},
    y: {domain: [0, 1], label: "false-alarm rate", tickFormat: "%"},
    color: {domain: ["Pairwise t-tests", "ANOVA"], range: [c.alt, c.fn], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: c.muted}),
      Plot.lineY(rows, {x: "k", y: "rate", stroke: "procedure", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(rows, {
        x: "k", y: "rate", fill: "procedure", r: 3.5,
        title: d => d.procedure === "ANOVA"
          ? `k = ${d.k}: one F-test, ${(100 * d.rate).toFixed(0)}%`
          : `k = ${d.k}: ${d.m} tests, 1 − 0.95^${d.m} = ${(100 * d.rate).toFixed(1)}%`
      })
    ]
  }))
}
```
